question: Can the 14 fish-name strings in the abstract of Mallari et al. (2020) be compared with current fish-name records without silently correcting or validating the source's specimens?

method.nameAuthority: California Academy of Sciences, Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes; indexed record excerpts and name-specific queries checked 2026-11-26.
method.secondaryCrossChecks: ITIS Arius dispar record and Balisco & Liao (2025) annotated checklist of fish species described from the Philippines.
method.procedure: Compared each abstract-listed label preserved verbatim in the source review against an exact or closest current catalog record. Space insertion and spelling changes are recorded as candidate crosswalks only. No automatic matcher output or Catalog distribution statement was treated as a Candaba occurrence.
method.accessLimit: Catalog record text was reviewed from official indexed excerpts/search results; direct page access was not available for every selected record. No bulk Catalog export, local page snapshot, source article table, or specimen image was copied.

crosswalkCandidates.identityStatus: The Catalog states that the species is definitely known only from Java and is introduced elsewhere, citing Ng & Kottelat (2008). This is a voucher-review flag, not proof that the paper's identification is wrong or that the species is absent from Candaba.

The Catalog gives the native range as the Orinoco basin and says it is introduced elsewhere. The paper's Hito-to-Hypostomus mapping therefore needs voucher-level review; this distribution note does not disprove the source identification.

crossSourceFindings.sourceReportedCountConflict: The abstract lists 14 names; a body passage counts five Cyprinidae plus ten species from other families. The name crosswalk does not resolve that 14-versus-15 conflict.
crossSourceFindings.higherRiskNameAssignments: Clarias batrachus and Hypostomus plecostomus have biogeographic/introduced-range flags in the Catalog, and the paper maps the common name Hito to Hypostomus plecostomus. These require voucher or expert review; the broad range notes do not prove either presence or absence in Candaba.

limitations: The paper reports one representative specimen per species group deposited at the PSAU Biology Museum but provides no accession/catalog numbers or specimen-to-source-label crosswalk.
The paper gives no collection dates, effort-standardized dataset, or taxon-by-barangay matrix; no current presence or full-wetland checklist is established.
A valid or candidate current name does not independently re-identify a source specimen or establish occurrence, abundance, habitat, catchability, diet, safety, legal access, or bait advice.
The publisher declares CC BY-SA 4.0 for the article. No article table or figure was copied, and no Bangwit data-package ShareAlike compatibility review was performed.
nextActions: If PSAU museum material becomes accessible, request the accession numbers and independently compare labels or diagnostic material before resolving the higher-risk assignments.
Keep the abstract/body count mismatch and absent taxon-by-barangay mapping open; do not convert the 14 candidate crosswalks into a Candaba species checklist.
Continue separate historical-source searches for Candaba and other Central Luzon wetlands, lakes, rivers, and estuaries.

sources.supports: The official publisher item page, DOI, abstract and 14 source-reported taxon strings.
The publisher-hosted paper and its source-reported methods, museum deposit, common-name mapping, and count discrepancy.
